Subject: SignalPath post-call: throughput & latency recap + next technical steps

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the deep dive today. Quick recap & agreed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain you described:
- Real-time inference SLA: 95th pct tail must be under 180ms for single-turn user queries during peak (estimated 450 RPS).
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume reranking pipelines; current infra spend is the biggest blocker to scaling.
- Need for deterministic fallbacks: if the primary model has a degradation, route to a lighter, quantized variant without user-facing error.

What we confirmed about workload and model requirements:
- Model family: medium-sized causal model (approx 20B dense / supports quantization to int8) for primary generation; separate 7B reranker for N-best scoring.
- Typical context window: 1.5–2k tokens. Peak seq length 3k for longer conversational histories (10% of traffic).
- KV cache reuse is high (70% prefix overlap) which makes prefix caching viable.

Latency & throughput SLOs discussed:
- Target: 95p < 180ms; p99 < 400ms for gen model at 450 RPS burstable to 1k RPS for short windows.
- Throughput mode: batching for reranker (throughput-optimized), continuous-batch/pipeline for gen to keep tail low.

Operational topology we sketched:
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated pool (mixed A100 + L4i) with model-sharded serving and long-lived KV cache.
- Fallback: Quantized int8 variant on L4i nodes routed when queue depth exceeds threshold or if latency SLOs break.
- Cross-region: US primary with EU read-replicas for EU customers; routing by region and latency SLOs.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
1) Redwood: supply a short benchmark proposal + suggested test harness so you can run a controlled 450RPS -> 1kRPS burst (David) — by Thu 9/21.
2) SignalPath: provide sample representative payloads (anonymized) and expected N-best size for reranker; procurement will confirm process (Priya) — by Fri 9/22.
3) Tech sync: 60m calibration run planning (Karthik + Alex) to lock network topology, egress, and KV cache warmup strategy — propose Tue 9/26.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short proposal for latency benchmarking and an ops matrix for KV/cache strategies.

If anything above is off, flag it here and I’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll kick off the benchmark proposal and share the harness by Thursday.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

David — thanks for the crisp write-up. This matches our notes; a couple of clarifications below and two asks before the calibration run.

Clarifications:
- The 95p target of <180ms is for user-facing generation latency (single-turn). For multi-turn flows we can afford a slightly higher 95p (up to ~220ms) for context stitching.
- Reranker: N-best = 12 typically; we can produce smaller batches for high-frequency queries.

Asks before Tue 9/26 tech sync:
1) Can Redwood include an example JMeter/load script (or k6) as part of the harness so our infra team can run the same workload locally?
2) For the quantized fallback path, can you list the expected accuracy delta (top-1 vs baseline) from your internal hunts so we can run a quick regression?

We’ll get the anonymized payload set to you (Priya + Jordan owner) by 9/22. Procurement (Priya) will also outline any required DP addendums.

Alex
Alex Reyes
Head of ML Engineering | SignalPath

Quick technical notes from my side before the calibration run:

- Network egress: confirm whether SignalPath will allow long-lived TCP connections from our dedicated pool. Persistent connections + keep-alive are important to avoid cold-start penalties on KV cache.
- Batching strategy: for the gen model we should prefer very small, latency-aware micro-batches (size 1–4) with prefetch of KV entries. Reranker can batch up to 64 depending on token lengths.
- Quantization: our internal evals on similar 20B-family models show ~1.2–1.8% delta in top-1 accuracy moving from FP16->int8 with per-channel quant. I’ll attach a short extract of the quant eval.

I’ll be on the call Tue 9/26; if you want, I can draft the exact k6 scenario that mirrors the harness David will share.

Karthik
